Catalogue.x-meaning: The world source's own material vocabulary. emptyMaterialRef names the material that means an empty cell; it must be a key of materials.

HistoryEntries.x-order: committed history order; not name order

InventorySlots.x-order: engine slot order including empty strings

LightRule.x-meaning: minimumLight is normalised: 0 is the darkest and 1 the brightest light level the world source reports. The world source maps its own light scale onto it.

Ref.x-normalization: NONE; exact Unicode scalar sequence; never trim/lower/NFC; not a path

Revision.x-normalization: NONE; opaque equality, never numeric ordering

StateProfile.x-meaning: Declared by the world source for the state map of a Record. derivedFields are recomputed by the engine after a write and are never compared: the expected value is the readback value. preservedFields keep the before value when a cell is written. clearedFields are absent after a cell is written. The three sets are disjoint; a field in none of them is not expected to exist after a write.

ChunkPosition.x-order: partition cell x,y,z = floor(position/partition.edge) per axis

RegionRuns.x-order: VoxelArea index order: x fastest, then y, then z

RegionLighting.x-meaning: Light recalculation fact of a world source that declares postWriteLighting REQUIRED. method is the world source's opaque name for how it recalculated.

ClearanceCells.description: Building design clearance proposed by the skill and confirmed by the player. Not a measured, templated or derived player size; it does not prove that a real player fits.

BuildDimensions.description: Building size in whole nodes chosen by the player. Not a player or avatar size.

ProtectionPrincipal.description: Basis of a CELL_PROTECTION check. ANONYMOUS: the engine asks the game's protection with no caller identity (for example core.is_protected(pos, '')), so every protected cell is refused for everyone, owners included; it is not acting-principal protection. ACTING_PRINCIPAL: the check runs for a trusted identity of the acting player; no such identity source exists in this major.

EngineGuardDeclaration.description: What the loaded engine payload actually checks, per guard and per stage. A stage not listed is not covered; nothing is implied by a name or a package version.

GuardRefusal.description: Why an engine guard refused, carried beside the Error it explains. BODY_OCCUPIED/PROTECTED_CELL/PLAYER_ENCLOSED are violations of BODY_CLEARANCE/CELL_PROTECTION/PLAYER_ENCLOSURE; GUARD_UNAVAILABLE means the stage needed the guard and it is not covered (RESTORE_GUARD_UNAVAILABLE = BODY_CLEARANCE at RESTORE).

OpaqueValue.x-meaning: Any strict JSON value owned by the world source. Carried and digested unchanged; never interpreted outside the world source.

OpaqueCode.x-normalization: NONE; exact Unicode scalar sequence; never trim/lower/NFC; not a path
OpaqueCode.x-meaning: A reason code defined by the world source. Consumers show or relay it; they never branch on its value.

Orientation.x-meaning: Neutral orientation index of a material, from the set the Catalogue declares for that material. Conversion to an engine encoding happens only inside the world source.

MaterialTags.x-meaning: Neutral tags the world source normalises from its own material definitions. placeable is the world source's conclusion that the material can be written and restored on its declared write path with no side effect and no persistent state; null is unknown and never treated as false or true. Raw engine fields stay in extension and are never read outside the world source.

EngineRevisions.x-meaning: Opaque revisions the world source reports for what defines its materials. Compared for equality only.

WriteBackendRef.x-meaning: Opaque identity of the world source's write backend. Compared for equality only.

GeometryProfile.x-meaning: Geometry profile of a payload. This major defines only voxel-grid/v1: integer grid positions, closed integer boxes, one material per cell. Another profile is a new variant added beside it, never a change of this one. A payload whose profile the world source does not declare is refused with CAPABILITY_GAP, never guessed.

Partition.x-meaning: The world source's storage partition of a voxel-grid world: cells are grouped into boxes of edge[x,y,z] cells aligned at multiples of edge on each axis. Region payloads are cut along it. Declared by the world source; never assumed.

PostWriteLighting.x-meaning: REQUIRED: after a region write the world source recalculates light for the written box and reports a RegionLighting fact; a VERIFIED region commit or undo needs it COMPLETE. NONE: the world source has no separate light pass; no lighting fact exists and none is checked.

WorldGeometry.x-meaning: What the world source declares about its geometry. geometryProfiles is open: it may name profiles this contracts major does not define, and a payload profile absent from it is a CAPABILITY_GAP. partition is non-null exactly when voxel-grid/v1 is declared.

SrgbColor.x-meaning: An sRGB colour as lower-case #rrggbb. The world source decides how it is obtained (declared, or from its own assets); consumers compare and match colours only.

MaterialPresentation.x-meaning: How the world source names and colours one material for people and for image material matching. null is unknown, never a default name or colour.

OrientationDescriptor.x-meaning: Neutral meaning of one orientation index: clockwise quarter turns about the Frame up axis seen from above, and whether the material is flipped upside down. null means the world source has no neutral expression for that part; the conversion to an engine encoding stays inside the world source.

WriteMethods.x-meaning: The write methods the world source supports on the paired connection. A method not listed is not supported; nothing is implied by a package or wire version.

EngineFrame.x-meaning: The world source coordinate frame: axis directions, handedness and grid unit. A Frame for one target adds origin and revision.

AvatarSize.x-meaning: Extent in Frame grid units: width along x, height along the up axis, depth along z.

AvatarEnvelope.x-meaning: The body envelope the world source declares for its player body: a fixed size it vouches for, the same for every player and every moment. Never a live position, yaw, posture or identity; players joining, leaving or moving never change it. UNAVAILABLE/NO_PUBLIC_SOURCE when the world source declares none; consumers then refuse by name, never fill a size.

SideEffectConclusion.x-meaning: The world source conclusion for its declared write path. hasSideEffects: writing (or restoring) runs engine behaviour beyond setting material and orientation. hasPersistentState: the write can leave per-cell state that a readback must account for. null is unknown and is never treated as false or true.

SideEffectConclusionMap.x-meaning: materialRef -> conclusion. A material that is absent is unknown.

WritePathConclusions.x-meaning: Write path conclusions derived inside the world source from its own engine. path covers what fires for every write on the path; materials covers each material definition. Contracts derive nothing from engine callback names here.

CatalogueFacts.x-meaning: The world source material vocabulary with names, colours and the neutral orientation index. presentation has exactly the Catalogue materials as keys; orientationIndex describes every orientation any material declares.

MaterialSourceFacts.x-meaning: Material sources and colours for image material selection. presentation has exactly the materialRefs of snapshot.materials as keys. Texture bytes are not on the wire: they are referenced by bytesDigest and travel through the in-process material sources port.

EngineFacts.x-meaning: Geometry, partition, bounds, frame, lighting and write facts the world source declares for the paired connection. engineBounds null means the world source declares no bound.

WriteProfile.x-meaning: Everything a host needs to forward for writing: opaque write backend, the complete compilation configuration, supported write methods and the body envelope. compilationConfig is non-null exactly when writeBackend is KNOWN and then carries that writeBackend unchanged. A host forwards it as is: it never interprets, completes or defaults a field.

WorldSourceCapabilities.x-meaning: One read of what the world source (owner is the role, never a package) declares for the paired connection: geometry and partition, bounds, state field rules, post-write lighting, write backend and compilation configuration, write methods, write path conclusions, the guards it covers and the body envelope. engineGuards null means no guard is covered.

InspectionContext.x-meaning: The world and selection the session is currently bound to, as the host bridge holds them. localContext.worldRef equals worldRef.

worldRoot.description: Provider-owned local root locator; owning runtime canonicalizes it. Not a world reference.

LocalWorldsSourceDescription.description: Read-only current locator for the exact requested worldRef. Interpreted only inside the paired adapter/local-runtime world source; grants no launch/write/delete authority and never enters host C-world-lifecycle fields.

PluginRole.x-meaning: A HanaWorlds plugin role. A role is filled by whichever plugins register the contract evidence pluginRoles.evidence names for it, never by package name or configuration.

PluginRolesStatus.x-meaning: COMPLETE: every required role has a provider. PARTIAL: some required roles have a provider and missingRoles names the rest. UNAVAILABLE: the read succeeded and no required role has a provider. A failed read is never a status; it is the response error.

PluginRoleProviders.x-meaning: Role -> plugins currently providing it, each named by its loader module specifier (moduleName), sorted by code unit, no duplicates. An empty array means the role has no provider in the running host. One plugin may appear under several roles; one role may list several plugins. No versions (versions stay with remote.pluginManager.listBundles).

PluginRoles.x-meaning: missingRoles is exactly the required roles whose providers are empty, in pluginRoles.roles order.
